title: First Messy Play
strapline: A soft blob of gloop, a smear of foam, a puddle of paint — the littlest hands meeting the joy and mess of it all.
intent: Give babies their very first messy, tactile play — soft, safe, single materials to smear, pat, poke and squish.
Offer the pure sensory joy of the substance itself: the coolness of gloop, the fluff of foam, the slither of soap flakes.
Build the earliest mark-making as hands drag through foam and paint, leaving trails that appear and vanish.
Support babies who find mess overwhelming to explore at their own pace — a fingertip today, a whole hand next week.
Keep every session close, calm and led by the baby, so first mess feels safe and delightful, never forced.
implementation: Offer one soft material at a time on a tray or highchair top: cornflour gloop, whipped soap flakes, baby-safe foam, natural yoghurt paint.
Sit close and let the baby set the pace — some dive in, some watch, some touch with one careful finger; all of it is fine.
Never plunge a reluctant baby's hands in; offer a spoon, a brush or a tiny taste of the material on your own fingers first.
Narrate the sensation as the baby explores ('so soft and fluffy — look at the trail your finger made').
Use only baby-safe, ideally taste-safe materials for this age, supervise closely, and keep a warm flannel and towel right there.
key_questions: What does the foam feel like on your fingers?
Look at the line you drew — where has it gone?
Shall we touch it together, just a little bit?
Is it cold, or warm, or somewhere in between?
You patted it and it splatted — did you like that?

impact.text: Babies explore paint, foam and gloop for the sheer joy of the sensation, patting, smearing and squishing.
A baby drags fingers and whole hands through the material, making the first appearing-and-vanishing marks.
Babies meet the messy materials with hands and mouth, finding out what soft, cool and slippery are.
With a calm adult close, even a cautious baby explores mess at their own pace and returns for more.

enhancements: Whipped soap flakes — cloud-soft, safe and utterly inviting to pat.
Cornflour gloop that flows off the fingers and firms under a poke.
A foam-and-mirror tray, so smears and reflections meet.
Natural yoghurt paint in one soft colour for first fingertip marks.
A brush, a spoon or a sponge for the baby who prefers a tool to bare hands at first.

playing_exploring: The baby explores the material freely, at their own pace and in their own way.
Touch and sight lead — the substance is patted, smeared, poked and watched.
active_learning: A cautious baby grows braver session by session, from one fingertip to two hands deep.
creating_thinking: Babies notice cause and effect — I patted it and it splatted, I dragged it and a line appeared.
